professional: a senior control engineer reviewing for a sampled-data / digital-control venue (e.g. IEEE Control Systems Letters or an IFAC conference); they check first that the ZOH discretisation and the Jury reduction are right, then that the inter-sample behaviour (not only samples) is measured, then that the deadbeat and pole-placement gains match the textbook (Franklin, Powell & Workman; Astrom & Wittenmark), then what is new relative to the classical digital-PD stability-region literature

evidence.correctness: Independent recomputation in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/81df4cd4-800b-55c5-bc31-b22ef2785d5d/scratchpad/st/indep.py (numpy only, none of the author's code): ZOH discretisation by Van Loan augmented matrix exponential, eigenvalues by numpy.linalg.eigvals, Jury conditions re-derived by hand (1-tr+det = kpT^2, 1+tr+det = 4-2kdT, det<1 iff kd>kpT/2). Bisection on numpy eigenvalue modulus gives critical wnT 1, 2, 1.428571, 1, 0.5, 0.25 for zeta 0.25..4, identical to min(4z,1/z) and results.txt. Pole moduli at zeta=0.7, wnT 0.5/1/1.2/1.3/1.4: 0.65192/0.31623/0.2/0.625/0.91822, identical. Textbook Mp exp(-pi z/sqrt(1-z^2)) = 0.04599 (0.0460). Closed-form twin settle 6.4081 (6.407/6.408). Deadbeat K=[1/T^2, 3/(2T)] from FPW gives (A-BK)^2 = 0 exactly; Ackermann for rho=0.8, phi=0.3, T=0.2 gives kpT^2 0.1115, kdT 0.4157 (identical). Real settle at wnT 1.3/1.4/1.0 = 14.3/72.8/4.0 and at T=0.1 wn=10/14 = 0.4/5.2, identical. The one discrepancy: inter-sample overshoot is sampled at m=20 points per period instead of at the parabola's vertex, so it is under-read in the 4th printed digit (wnT 1.2: 0.2341 vs exact 0.2343; 1.4: 0.4847 vs 0.4852). Everything else matches to the printed precision; 3 not 4 because of that and because it is a textbook-sized model.

Five mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 2 caught (design_poles kd divisor 2->2.1; critical_wnT 1/zeta -> 1.05/zeta), 3 survived (overshoot evaluated only at the period end, i.e. inter-sample excursion ignored; settle_time on |x| instead of the state norm; settle_time off by one sample). The settling and overshoot metrics behind result sections 2 and 3 are untested except for the unstable->inf case and a T=1e-3 overshoot check that cannot see inter-sample effects. The 'independent RK4 check' is exact by construction for a polynomial flow (model.py:72 says so), so test_step_matrix_matches_rk4 and section 1's RK4 column compare two exact forms of the same map.
evidence.craft: Read src/sample_twin/model.py (115 lines), tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py, experiments/figure.py. Small, pure stdlib, readable, docstrings state definitions. Defects: inter_sample_extremes (model.py:83-92) grids 20 points where the minimum of the quadratic x+v tau+u tau^2/2 is available in closed form at tau=-v/u; inter_sample_extremes ignores a nonzero v0 although simulate takes one; simulate_rk4 duplicates simulate under an 'independent' label.
evidence.claims: Checked every numeric claim in README.md line 3 and paper/whitepaper.md results 1-4 against results.txt and the independent recomputation: all match (boundary values, 4.40 samples per period, 0.0460->0.0463, 6.41 vs 6.30, 0.234, 14.3, 72.8, 247, settling series 6.3..10.2, instability from 14.3, deadbeat (1.1e-16, 0), 2T=0.4, '5x at 1.2' = 0.234/0.046=5.09, 'within 0.0007'). Limits and stylisation are stated in both files; the paper says the Jury reduction is classical. Two misstatements: README:3 says 'the twin's pole modulus e^{-zeta wn T} is optimistic: at wnT = 1.2 ...' but at 1.2 the real modulus is 0.200 vs the twin's 0.432, i.e. the twin is pessimistic about decay there (it is optimistic only from about 1.25; the paper's result 2 states this correctly); paper:13 rounds 0.65192 to 0.651.
evidence.fitness: A researcher on the twin-fidelity family (timestep-twin, latency-twin) gets a clean, verified baseline. But the result is not new: closed-form stability regions for digital PD on rigid (double-integrator) and flexible plants via Jury critical constraints are published (Al-Salem et al., 'Stability analysis for digital PD control of flexible systems', found by WebSearch), and deadbeat for the ZOH double integrator is a standard course exercise (e.g. UCSB ECE147B module 6) and textbook example (FPW). The paper does not cite that digital-PD literature and offers no question beyond the textbook; against the PhD/publishable bar in research/CLAUDE.md it is a worked example, not a contribution.
evidence.domain: The method is the standard one a control engineer uses (exact ZOH discretisation, Jury, direct discrete pole placement, inter-sample overshoot), and conclusions agree with practice (twin adequate for wnT <~ 0.2, consistent with the Astrom & Wittenmark sampling rules of thumb, which are not cited). Departures a reviewer would flag: no computation delay (the dominant practical effect; named in Limitations), inter-sample overshoot gridded rather than exact, settling metric sampled.

defects.what: The settling and inter-sample overshoot metrics that carry results 2 and 3 are untested on any stable non-trivial case: three seeded bugs (overshoot only at samples, settle on |x| not the norm, settle off by one sample) leave all 8 tests green.

Novelty: the Jury stability region of digital PD on a double integrator and the deadbeat gains are classical (textbooks; Al-Salem et al. on digital PD stability regions; standard coursework). The paper cites the textbooks but not the digital-PD stability-region literature and poses no question beyond them; below the PhD/publishable bar of research/CLAUDE.md.

README says the twin's pole modulus is optimistic and cites wnT = 1.2, where the real modulus (0.200) is less than half the twin's (0.432); the twin is optimistic only from about wnT 1.25 (the paper's result 2 gets this right).

Inter-sample overshoot is evaluated on a 20-point grid per period instead of at the quadratic's vertex, under-reading printed values in the 4th digit (0.2341 vs exact 0.2343 at wnT 1.2; 0.4847 vs 0.4852 at 1.4); it also ignores v0.

The 'independent RK4 held-input' check is exact for the polynomial flow (the code says so), so it re-derives the same map rather than independently checking it; presented as independent in README and paper result 1.
Paper rounds real pole modulus 0.65192 to 0.651.

verdict: Correct and reproducible: every boundary, pole modulus, settling time, deadbeat and pole-placement number recomputed independently with numpy (Van Loan ZOH, eigvals, Ackermann, closed-form twin) matches results.txt, except a 4th-digit under-read of inter-sample overshoot from a 20-point grid; run.py and figure.py reproduce the committed outputs byte for byte. It does not meet the bar: verification is 2 (3 of 5 seeded bugs in the settling and overshoot metrics survive), and as research it is a clean worked textbook example (Jury region of sampled PD, deadbeat) rather than a new result, with the digital-PD stability-region literature uncited. One README sentence misstates the pole-modulus comparison at wnT 1.2.
